breach_title: The 2019 Capital One Cloud Data Breach
attacker: Paige Thompson (alias 'erratic', former AWS software engineer)

impact.individuals_affected: Approx. 106 Million (100M US residents, 6M Canadian residents)
impact.data_compromised: 140,000 Social Security numbers, 80,000 linked bank account numbers, 1 Million Canadian Social Insurance Numbers, millions of credit scores, limits, balances, and payment histories.
impact.financial_penalties: $80 Million regulatory fine by the OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency), $190 Million customer class action settlement, and over $300 Million in total incident remediation costs.

root_causes.name: SSRF Vulnerability in WAF / Reverse Proxy
root_causes.summary: An open-source Web Application Firewall (ModSecurity) running on an Amazon EC2 instance had a misconfigured proxy feature that allowed external requests to be redirected to internal services without host/IP validation.

root_causes.name: Reliance on Unprotected AWS IMDSv1
root_causes.summary: The EC2 instance was using AWS Instance Metadata Service version 1 (IMDSv1). In IMDSv1, metadata is queried via plain HTTP GET requests without session tokens. When an SSRF flaw existed, the attacker could easily fetch temporary STS security credentials.

root_causes.name: Excessive IAM Role Permissions (Violation of Least Privilege)
root_causes.summary: The IAM instance profile assigned to the WAF server (app-waf-role) was granted broad wildcard permissions (s3:* on *). A WAF has no business need to read or sync customer credit application S3 buckets.

root_causes.name: Lack of S3 Bucket Egress and VPC Endpoint Controls
root_causes.summary: Sensitive S3 buckets holding unencrypted or transparently decrypted customer records did not restrict access to specific VPC Endpoints or enforce Customer Managed KMS key policies that required secondary authorization.

defense_layers.solution: SSRF Input Validation and Link-Local Blacklisting
defense_layers.detail: Validate all incoming URLs, reject loopback (127.0.0.1) and link-local (169.254.169.254) addresses, or enforce domain allowlists.
Configure instances with HttpTokens=required and HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1. Requires a session-oriented PUT request with token header, neutralizing simple SSRF and proxy traversal.

defense_layers.solution: Principle of Least Privilege & Service Control Policies (SCPs)
defense_layers.detail: Limit the WAF EC2 role exclusively to CloudWatch logging actions. Implement explicit Deny statements for sensitive customer buckets.

defense_layers.solution: S3 Bucket Policies & KMS Envelope Encryption
defense_layers.detail: Enforce aws:sourceVpce conditions so bucket access is strictly limited to authorized VPC Endpoints, and require dedicated AWS KMS CMKs.

timeline.event: Attacker scans the internet for SSRF-vulnerable reverse proxies and discovers Capital One's EC2 ModSecurity instance.
Attacker executes SSRF against 169.254.169.254 to harvest temporary AWS STS credentials for the 'WAFF-Role'.
Using the stolen credentials, the attacker lists ~700 S3 buckets and executes 'aws s3 sync' to exfiltrate credit applications.
A security researcher spots GitHub posts containing the exfiltrated bucket commands and alerts Capital One's security team.
FBI arrests the suspect; Capital One publicly discloses the incident.
AWS launches IMDSv2 globally to protect EC2 instance metadata from SSRF vulnerabilities.
